description: Future-proof education grant-domain terminology. Covers ESSA Title I-IV, Perkins V CTE, IDEA, competency-based education, and arts-integration framings. Drawn from ED, OESE, and OSEP program guidance. Starter pack — needs operator deepening for state-level program detail (PA Title I LEA processes, special-pop subgranting).

domains.name: ESSA program titles
domains.description: Every Student Succeeds Act (2015) funding streams: I (disadvantaged), II (educator quality), III (English learners), IV (well-rounded + safe + tech).

domains.name: Career & technical education + alternative pathways
domains.description: Perkins V, competency-based education, 21st Century Community Learning Centers, credit recovery.

domains.name: Special populations
domains.description: IDEA Part B/C, Title III ELs, McKinney-Vento (homeless), foster, migrant — populations with dedicated funding + reporting requirements.

facts.statement: ESSA Title I (Improving Basic Programs Operated by LEAs) is the largest K-12 federal funding stream, distributed by formula to LEAs based on poverty count. Schoolwide programs require ≥40% poverty enrollment; targeted-assistance programs serve identified students at any school. Title I plans must include: (1) needs assessment, (2) evidence-based interventions (Tier 1-4 per ESSA evidence definitions), (3) parent + family engagement plan. Tier 1 = strong evidence; Tier 4 = demonstrates rationale.

ESSA Title II Part A (Supporting Effective Instruction) funds educator preparation, professional development, recruitment, and retention. Allowable uses: PD aligned to academic standards, induction programs for new teachers, leadership pathways. Reviewers expect: needs-driven (cite educator-survey or evaluation data), evidence-based (Tier 1-3), measurable PD outcome (not seat-time). Avoid vendor-product-specific framing — funder neutrality requirement.

ESSA Title IV Part A (Student Support and Academic Enrichment Grants, SSAEG) funds three pillars: (1) well-rounded education (arts, civics, STEM, AP, dual-enrollment), (2) safe and healthy schools (mental health, bullying prevention, nutrition), (3) effective use of technology (≤15% of allocation on tech infrastructure). LEAs receiving ≥$30K must split ≥20% to (1), ≥20% to (2), and tech is capped. Strong proposals show all three pillars represented.

ESSA defines four evidence tiers for interventions: Tier 1 (Strong) = at least one well-designed RCT showing positive effect; Tier 2 (Moderate) = at least one quasi-experimental study with positive effect; Tier 3 (Promising) = correlational study with statistical controls; Tier 4 (Demonstrates Rationale) = logic model + ongoing evaluation. Title I, II, IV proposals must cite the evidence tier for each proposed intervention. WhatWorksClearinghouse (WWC) is the reviewer-expected source.

Carl D. Perkins Career and Technical Education Act (Perkins V, 2018) is the primary federal CTE funding stream. State plans submitted every 4 years; LEAs receive subgrants via formula or RFP. Reserve fund (≤15% state allocation) supports innovation + rural CTE. Programs of Study must be sequenced + non-duplicative, lead to industry-recognized credential, articulate to postsecondary. Comprehensive Local Needs Assessment (CLNA) every 2 years, conducted with stakeholder input including students + parents.

Competency-Based Education (CBE) advances students based on demonstrated mastery of competencies, not seat-time. ED-favored framing: (1) student-paced progression, (2) clear measurable competencies, (3) flexible support including RPL, (4) assessment is meaningful + diagnostic. CBE has explicit support in ESSA Title I Section 1003(g) (school-improvement) and Title IV Part F. Reviewers expect: competency framework cited (e.g., state-developed or Aurora Institute), assessment validity discussion, equity-of-pacing safeguards.

21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC, ESSA Title IV Part B) funds out-of-school-time programming (afterschool, summer) for students at high-poverty / low-performing schools. Allowable activities: academic enrichment, tutoring, STEM, arts, mental health, family engagement. Programs must operate ≥12 hrs/week during school year. Strong proposals: braid academic + enrichment, document family + community partner engagement, propose specific OST attendance + behavior outcome metrics.

Credit recovery = mechanism for students who failed a course to regain credit toward graduation, typically via competency demonstration or accelerated re-enrollment. ED has flagged poor-quality online credit-recovery as a risk to graduation-rate validity (especially in NCLB-era studies); strong proposals frame credit recovery with (1) substantive instruction not just test-out, (2) certified-teacher of record, (3) progress-monitoring data, (4) post-recovery academic outcome tracking. Avoid 'self-paced computer modules' framing without instructional design specifics.

Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) Part B serves children 3-21 (school-age special education); Part C serves infants/toddlers 0-3 (early intervention, state-administered). Federal share is formula-distributed but ED has never funded the originally-promised 40% excess-cost share — typical actual federal share is 10-13%. LEA proposals leveraging IDEA must respect maintenance-of-effort requirement (LEA can't reduce special-ed spending year-over-year). Discretionary IDEA funds (Part D) support state-program improvement, technical assistance, parent training.

ESSA Title III (English Language Acquisition) funds programs for English learners (ELs) and immigrant children/youth. Formula based on EL count + immigrant population. Title III subgrants must supplement, not supplant, state/local EL services. State plans must define EL entry + exit criteria using ELP standards + assessment. Strong proposals: cite the state ELP assessment (e.g., WIDA ACCESS), describe co-teaching / sheltered-instruction model, address dual-language vs ESL programmatic choice with rationale.

McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act guarantees homeless children/youth: immediate enrollment without proof-of-residence, school-of-origin choice with transportation, full participation in school activities. Each LEA must designate a Homeless Liaison. ED counts ~1.2M+ homeless students annually (2020-21 data). Strong proposals: identify Liaison capacity, describe identification practices (often dramatically undercounted), connect to wraparound supports. Sub-population framing: 'doubled up' (largest), shelter, unsheltered, hotel/motel.

Arts integration = teaching academic content through and with arts disciplines (not arts-as-elective). Distinct from STEAM (STEM + Arts) which is a curriculum-positioning frame. ESSA Title IV-A 'well-rounded education' explicitly includes arts. Strong proposals: cite a specific arts-integration model (Kennedy Center CETA, Drew Charter School, Turnaround Arts), name partner arts organizations, propose teaching-artist + classroom-teacher co-planning structure, measure both academic + arts outcome.

relationships.description: Title I schoolwide and targeted-assistance plans must cite ESSA evidence tier for proposed interventions.
Perkins V Programs of Study with industry credentials are well-suited to CBE pacing — competencies map to credential requirements.
21st CCLC out-of-school-time funding is a common vehicle for arts-integration pilots given the well-rounded enrichment framing.
Title I Set-Aside funds (≥$ varies) are required to support McKinney-Vento-eligible students; LEAs must document the calculation.
